purpose: Understand structured forecasting and verify CPU training/export/inference; no state-of-the-art claim
target: Total rentals in the next source-calendar hour
clocks: Naive source-local date/hour labels; no asserted UTC or DST reconstruction. Assume the previous completed hour count is immediately available. This is a retrospective forecast, not an operational service.
missing_hours: Require 48 consecutive observed input hours plus the immediately following target hour; exclude windows crossing gaps; never impute missing counts
architecture: Existing one pre-norm block, four attention heads, exact GELU MLP, final layer norm, fixed window-relative sinusoidal positions; dropout zero
split_policy: Target hour start in [split_start, split_end); past context may precede split start; no random cross-split shuffle
scaler: Population mean/std of unique rows used in training inputs only; constant feature scale=1; frozen embedded FP32
initialization: Seeded Xavier body, zero output head; epoch 0 repeats the latest rental count and is an eligible candidate
loss: MSE of standardized next-hour rental count
selection: Earliest minimum validation MAE among epochs 0..8; all seeds and baselines sealed before test evaluation
ridge_objective: Mean squared residual + alpha * squared coefficients; train-only centering/scaling and unpenalized intercept
ridge_selection: Minimum validation MAE; first alpha wins ties

uncertainty.method: paired day-cluster bootstrap of absolute-error difference; resample whole source-calendar days

demonstration_gate: All three selected models reduce test MAE by at least 10% versus last hour; primary seed's paired interval upper bound below zero. This is a learning demonstration, not a claim to outperform every baseline.
forecast_postprocessing: None: no clipping, rounding or test-dependent correction; report negative predictions
stopping: Exactly three seeds and eight epochs; no outcome-dependent extension, architecture change or feature search
limitations: Historical source-label gaps and uncertain publication delay
Day bootstrap does not capture longer seasonal dependence
Known public benchmark, not an untouched external evaluation
No financial, deployment or speed-frontier claim
